title: Cardinality-aware KV TTL and Batch Safety Playbook
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Deliver an operational playbook and automation prototype that tunes per-prefix TTLs and cache key shaping with direct awareness of prefix cardinality and batching behavior. This ticket captures modeling, safe apply/rollback automation, and lightweight runtime guards to prevent cost regressions or latency spikes. The approach emphasizes conservative economic thresholds, sampled shadow experiments, and a fast rollback path with minimal operator intervention.
acceptance_criteria:
1) TTL recommendations produced for top 95% of prefixes by cost impact with per-prefix metadata including estimated hit-rate delta, expected token savings, and risk score.
2) Automation runs a staged apply: shadow -> partial canary (1-5%) -> regional canary (10-25%) -> global apply, with automatic rollback triggers defined.
3) Rollback triggers include >5% p95 latency increase, >10% drop in application-level success rate, or net cost per 1M tokens increase beyond configured budget.
4) Documentation (runbook) and an operator CLI to preview, approve, and abort a rollout.
5) End-to-end test harness that simulates synthetic traffic with configurable cardinality to validate recommendations and rollback gates.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Data modeling (2 wks) - build prefix cardinality estimator using sampled logs and approximate counting (HyperLogLog), augment with request size distribution and batching behavior. Produce a cost impact model that combines hit-rate lift, batching improvements (reduction in per-token compute due to larger batches), and additional KV storage costs.
Phase 2: Recommendation engine (1 wk) - generate per-prefix TTL and key-shape suggestions ranked by expected ROI and risk score. Include a conservative default band (min, suggested, max) instead of a single value.
Phase 3: Safety automation (1 wk) - implement staged rollout automation integrated with canary gates: shadow traffic collection, metric diff computation, and automatic rollback policy. Use feature-flag driven application toggles or runtime config with gradual percentage ramps.
Phase 4: Runbook + operator UX (1 wk) - CLI/report to preview recommendations, toggle test runs, and trigger manual rollouts. Add links to dashboards and debug artifacts.
Phase 5: Pilot and iterate (2 wks) - run on two low-risk customers and one internal service; tune thresholds and heuristics before wider rollout.
rollout_plan:
1) Shadow evaluation (2 days): route 100% production reads to shadow TTL layer; collect hit/miss counts, latency, and batching distribution without affecting responses.
2) Small canary (1-3% user traffic, 48h): apply TTLs for ephemeral prefixes with low risk score. Monitor metrics and synth traffic.
3) Regional ramp (10-25%, 72h): expand to a region with lower traffic elasticity. If all gates pass, continue.
4) Global application (rolling over 1-2 weeks): apply TTLs in waves with automated monitoring and the ability to pause at each step.
5) Fast rollback: if any gate trips, revert config within 1 minute and continue a post-mortem.
Gate evaluation cadence: 5m for latency/cost, 1h for hit-rate stabilization.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: model math and HLL cardinality estimator.
- Integration tests: synthetic traffic generator that can vary prefix cardinality and batch sizes to validate model predictions vs observed hit-rate/batching lift.
- Chaos tests: introduce temporary KV availability degradation to ensure rollback works and clients degrade gracefully.
- A/B shadow tests: compare baseline vs TTL-applied cohorts for 48h windows.
- Performance tests: ensure no more than 1% increase in tail p95 under typical load during rollout.
- Regression tests: include previous autotune scenarios to ensure no negative interactions with existing cache autotuners.
metrics: Primary: cache hit-rate delta (absolute and relative), average tokens saved per 1M requests, net cost delta ($) per 1M tokens. Secondary: p50/p95 latency delta, request success rate, batch size distribution, KV ops/sec. Safety thresholds: p95 latency +5%, success rate -1%, cost delta +10% -> automatic rollback. All metrics stored in Grafana with per-canary breakdown.
comments: 2025-02-18 Avery Chen: Initial ticket created. Focus on cardinality because many prefixes have extreme skew and naive TTLs either over-evict or bloat cache storage.
2025-02-20 Diego Márquez: Ran a 24h sample analysis across 3 services; top 2% prefixes account for ~68% of KV lookups. Planning HLL for cardinality. See analysis notebook: GDrive link in 'links'.
2025-02-25 Design review: Request to add a UI preview that shows recommended TTL bands and explains risk in plain language for on-call engineers.

2025-02-28 Engineering note: Implementing a batching-aware term in the ROI model — if average batch size increases by >=10% for a prefix, the per-token cost reduction estimate is significant and raises ROI ranking.

2025-03-03 Diego Márquez: Shadow harness deployed on staging; initial shadow run shows predicted hit-rate lift within 8% of observed for medium-cardinality prefixes. High-cardinality prefixes show more variance; flagging for conservative min TTLs.
2025-03-04 Avery Chen: Added safety gating thresholds and rollback SLA to the ticket. Next: write rollout automation prototype and operator runbook.
notes: Design decision: use HLL for cardinality estimate to keep memory overhead small and computation cheap when running recommendations across millions of prefixes.

Trade-off: aggressive TTL increases reduce hit-rate risk for low-cardinality prefixes but can cause large variance for high-cardinality prefixes; we bias recommendations towards conservative increases for high-cardinality groups.
Fallback: when in doubt, prefer widening TTL band (min/suggested/max) and require manual approval for max value on sensitive prefixes.
Operator ergonomics: provide a dry-run CLI output that includes simulated cost delta and 95% confidence intervals before applying changes.
